filter.description: One filter rule. Rules on the same column are OR-ed (a row matching any of them is kept); rules on different columns are AND-ed. range keeps start <= value < end, i.e. [start, end): the end itself is excluded, so to keep the column maximum (or any row equal to end) add last: true. category keeps the listed level(s).

value.description: category filter: the level to keep (compared as its label; null = missing), or a list of levels (any of them)

last.description: range only: true includes end, [start, end] instead of [start, end); needed whenever end is the column maximum

filters.description: same column: OR; different columns: AND. range is [start, end) unless last: true

constraints.rule: filters[].kind='range' is half-open [start, end); set last=true whenever end equals the column maximum. Same-column rules OR; different columns AND.

capabilities.description: Rule-based deep statistics: strong correlations, skew/outliers, ANOVA hints, hypotheses.

Rule-based next-step recommendations with runnable targets (run_target = {tool, args}). Optional goal (compare_groups, relationship, distribution, process_stability, process_capability, measurement_system, summarize_variables) returns an ordered path for that purpose; a step with needs[] lacks values only the user knows (e.g. lsl/usl). Without goal the general recommendations are returned. goals[] lists the purposes.

goal.description: optional purpose; gives an ordered analysis path for it: compare_groups (그룹 비교); relationship (관계 파악); distribution (분포 확인); process_stability (공정 안정성); process_capability (공정능력); measurement_system (측정 시스템); summarize_variables (변수 요약)

capabilities.description: Render one of 17 plots: writes a PNG to workspace/plots/ and returns its path plus chart_data (every drawn number), so the figure can be read without seeing the image; params.include_image adds a PNG data URI. Put every option (axis, sampling, caption, ...) inside params, never next to it; params lists the options each operation takes.

params.description: Every option goes inside params, including axis, sampling, caption, group_x/group_y and include_image; only dataset_id, operation, params and filters sit at the top level (any other top-level key is refused). Options of the chosen operation; a key the operation does not take is an error that lists the allowed ones. Keys by operation: histogram: bins, color, group, x, y; scatter: color, group, point_alpha, point_size, size, x, y; line: color, group, x, y; area: color, group, x, y; bar: agg, color, group, stat, statistic, x, y; grouped_bar: agg, color, group, stat, statistic, x, y; box: color, group, x, y; control_chart: column, value, x, y; qq_plot: column, x, y; residual_plot: x, y; capability_histogram: bins, column, lsl, usl, x, y; pca_scores: color, columns, group; scree_plot: columns, components; factor_scree_plot: columns, components; factor_loading_heatmap: columns, factors; pca_loading_heatmap: columns, components; crosstab_heatmap: column, group, row, x, y. Every operation also takes axis, caption, group_x, group_y, include_image, preview, sampling.

x.description: x column(s); several columns give one panel per x/y pair [area, bar, box, capability_histogram, control_chart, crosstab_heatmap, grouped_bar, histogram, line, qq_plot, residual_plot, scatter]

y.description: y (measured) column(s) [area, bar, box, capability_histogram, control_chart, crosstab_heatmap, grouped_bar, histogram, line, qq_plot, residual_plot, scatter]

color.description: one nominal/ordinal column that colours the marks (legend) [area, bar, box, grouped_bar, histogram, line, pca_scores, scatter]

group.description: alias of color [area, bar, box, crosstab_heatmap, grouped_bar, histogram, line, pca_scores, scatter]

size.description: one continuous column that sizes the points [scatter]

stat.description: bar statistic: count (default), mean, sum or median [bar, grouped_bar]

value.description: the measured column [control_chart]

column.description: the measured column (crosstab_heatmap: the column factor) [capability_histogram, control_chart, crosstab_heatmap, qq_plot]

columns.description: continuous columns (default: the first 8) [factor_loading_heatmap, factor_scree_plot, pca_loading_heatmap, pca_scores, scree_plot]

components.description: integer: number of components [factor_scree_plot, pca_loading_heatmap, scree_plot]

caption.description: up to 4 columns summarised under the figure [every operation]

include_image.description: true: also return the PNG as payload.image.data_uri [every operation]

preview.description: true: draw without recording (no history entry, no PNG file, result_id empty, image inline as payload.image.data_uri); the web UI's live preview uses it [every operation]

axis.description: every operation: axis ranges, scales, reference lines, marked areas, legend and grid

items.description: {axis: x|y (default y), value, label, color, style}
{axis: x|y (default x), start, end, color, alpha}

capabilities.description: Results recorded for a dataset, each with source (ui = done on the web UI's screens, agent = any other caller). since returns only results after that result id; source keeps one side; include_edits adds the table edit log (edits[]: revision, tool, change, source) and since_revision narrows it. Use it to see what the user changed in the web UI.

since.description: a result id; only later results are returned

since_revision.description: with include_edits: only edits that produced a later revision

capabilities.description: Label recorded results (result_ids) and table edits (revisions, from the edit log) with who made them; source defaults to ui. The web UI calls this for what is done on its screens, so an agent normally only reads the labels with history_list. The table and its revision are not changed.

Render a self-contained HTML report (workspace/reports/) from recorded results: report blocks (result blocks with comment/highlight/arrow overlays, text/comment/highlight blocks) in order, metric and record tables, embedded plot PNGs, a companion figure for each analysis (auto_figures, default on) and rule-based findings; returns the path, sections and findings (include_html also returns the HTML itself).
Save a dataset (values and modeling types), its history, the plot PNGs it references and a UI state as one project file in workspace/projects/.
Load a saved project (path from project_list) into a new dataset with its history, figures and UI state.
List saved projects, newest first.

Open the web UI of this workspace: reuse a running one (and open it in the browser), or return the command that starts it; never starts a process itself. When status is not running, run the returned background command in the folder this server was started in (its working directory; do not cd elsewhere), then call ui_open again. The UI is optional: every tool works without it.

constraints.rule: ui_open never spawns a server itself; when status != running, execute the returned command in the server's cwd then call ui_open again.

capabilities.description: Tell the open web UI what to show: open a dataset, switch to a tab, bring a recorded result into view (tab graph fills the Graph Builder with a plot result's roles), select columns of the table, show a short message. The directive is written to workspace/ui/show.json with the next sequence number and every open UI window with follow mode on applies it once, within a few seconds; called with no directive fields it only returns the latest directive. One-way: the agent never sees the screen.

constraints.rule: tab='graph' requires dataset_id and a result_id whose kind is 'plot' (non-plot stat results fail).
ui_show writes workspace/ui/show.json one-way; agent cannot observe the screen directly.

skill_config.description: Compiled OSAW statistical & quality workbench skill (v0.1.1, spec 21). Use when loading CSV/XLSX tables, running descriptive/inferential/multivariate/quality analyses, creating plots, synchronizing with the OSAW Web UI (ui_open, ui_show, history_list), or writing HTML reports.
execution_notes: MCP already provides every tool's input schema (`~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp/osaw/`). **Do NOT pre-read all preserved reference files**; open ONLY the single reference file needed for output schemas, verified results, failure cases, or parameter tables.
Prefer calling `dataset_profile` once per newly loaded dataset and checking `modeling_suggestions` before statistical routing (`platform_fit_y_by_x`).

Never shell out (`ls`) to relative `workspace/...` paths from the project root — the OSAW MCP server runs inside `osaw_workspace/`, so rely directly on MCP tool outputs (`bytes`, `path`, `result_id`, `seq`).
skill_config.rule_id_hints: e.g. R-FILT-01, R-PLOT-01, R-ASSUMP-01, R-UI-01, R-UI-02, R-UI-03, R-SPEC-01, R-MODEL-01, R-NO-FAKE-01, R-LANG-01, R-NUM-01
